question: Q2
prompt: I live in a municipality of the Brussels-Capital Region, hold valid residence and work authorization, and have worked full-time as a salaried employee for 4 years in Belgium. My employer has just ended my salaried employment contract in Brussels; I worked my notice period. I have never received unemployment benefits in Belgium before. I want to register as a jobseeker, apply for unemployment benefits, and possibly follow free vocational training in French or Dutch. Please state: (1) where and within what deadline I must register and apply for benefits, and how long I can receive them; (2) which bodies are responsible for job-seeker registration, benefit entitlement and payment, and vocational training; (3) how I can follow vocational training in French or Dutch without losing my benefits; and (4) the current official sources supporting your answer.
response_text:
Here is a complete, structured answer based on current official Belgian/Brussels sources (November 2026).

## 1. Where, within what deadline, and for how long

**Jobseeker registration (first step, mandatory before any benefit claim):**
Since you reside in the Brussels-Capital Region, you must register with **Actiris**. You must register within the eight days that follow your first day of unemployment, with the regional employment service of your Region — for the Brussels-Capital Region: Actiris. Since you worked your full notice period (not a "non-worked" notice), the 8-day deadline (not the 2-month deadline for non-worked notice) applies to you. Workers on non-worked notice have a maximum period of 2 months to register as jobseekers — but this does not apply to you since you worked the notice.

If you miss the 8-day deadline, you don't lose your rights entirely, but you will only be able to receive benefits from the day of your registration.

**Benefit application:**
You apply with a payment body (CAPAC/HVW or a union fund) — you must send the CAPAC: the C4 form (provided by your employer), the C1 form, and proof of registration as a jobseeker (with Actiris if domiciled in Brussels). There is no strict deadline for submitting the claim itself to your payment body, but your payment body then has a one-month deadline to transmit your file to the ONEM, which itself has 2 months to take a decision. Benefits are paid after verification by ONEM, which can take 2 to 4 weeks depending on the file. If accepted, you will be compensated starting from the date of your request, provided you registered on time.

**Duration of benefits — important recent reform:**
Belgium's traditionally unlimited unemployment benefit system has changed. The Belgian unemployment insurance system, previously atypical in Europe due to its unlimited duration of compensation, was significantly modified by the law of 18 July 2025, and the main measure of the reform is the limitation of the duration of unemployment benefit payments to 2 years. Concretely, under the new rules applicable from 1 March 2026: full unemployment benefits are limited to a maximum of 24 months (12 months of base entitlement and 12 additional months depending on professional background). More precisely, anyone who has worked at least one year in the last three years can claim one year of benefits, and each additional period of four months worked opens a right to one more month of benefits, within the absolute limit of two years. Given your 4 years of full-time salaried work, you should qualify for close to (or at) the 24-month maximum, but you should confirm your exact entitlement with Actiris/your payment body given the reform's transitional rules.

If your first claim is refused, you can lodge an appeal before the labour tribunal (tribunal du travail) within 3 months.

## 2. Responsible bodies

- **Jobseeker registration**: **Actiris** (the Brussels-Capital Region's public employment service) — the only competent regional body for residents of the Brussels-Capital Region.
- **Benefit entitlement decision**: **ONEM/RVA** (the National Employment Office), the federal body that examines and decides on your right to unemployment benefits.
- **Benefit payment**: a **payment institution** of your choice — either the **CAPAC/HVW** (the public auxiliary payment fund) or a **trade union** (FGTB, CSC, CGSLB) acting as payment agency. Payment institutions are the CAPAC or the unions.
- **Vocational training**: **Bruxelles Formation** (French-speaking) or **VDAB Brussel** (Dutch-speaking), Actiris's partner training bodies. For all French-language training in Brussels, contact Bruxelles Formation; for all Dutch-language training in Brussels, contact VDAB Brussel.

## 3. How to follow vocational training without losing benefits

You remain a registered jobseeker and keep benefits by obtaining a **"dispense de disponibilité" (availability waiver)** from Actiris:

- You must request a "dispense de disponibilité" (availability waiver), meaning you only need to remain partially available for the labour market.
- This waiver covers, among others, a vocational training from Bruxelles Formation, VDAB, Forem or ADG; with a waiver you remain registered as a jobseeker and must still follow the rules imposed by Actiris.
- Importantly, if you follow an approved vocational training, you automatically receive the waiver. For other types of studies/training/internships, you must actively request the waiver from Actiris.
- Timing matters: the dispensation request must be submitted before starting the studies, training or internship, and can be made directly with Actiris's Dispenses service (via MyActiris, email, or mail). If you go through your payment body instead, the request must be introduced before starting the studies, training or internship, with your payment institution (CAPAC or union), which will forward it to Actiris's Dispenses service.
- While on an approved vocational training with a waiver, your unemployment benefit is effectively frozen and your right to unemployment is extended — this is confirmed in an official ONEM factsheet.
- The training itself is free: training is free for jobseekers (via Bruxelles Formation); the same applies to VDAB Brussel's vocational courses. VDAB's vocational training is free, practice-oriented, adapted to the labour market and your skills.
- For language training specifically, Actiris itself offers free options: Actiris and VDAB offer jobseekers the possibility to follow a language course free of charge, e.g. via Actiris's "chèques langues," which can lead to an availability waiver too: under certain conditions, by following a language training you can benefit from an availability waiver in your job search.
- If you want a Dutch-language track with VDAB specifically, Actiris also runs a dedicated route: this can be done via a "Dutch-speaking professional project" with partner VDAB, open to all motivated jobseekers wanting to learn Dutch, regardless of their current level.

**Practical sequence**: (1) register with Actiris within 8 days → (2) submit C1/C4 to CAPAC or your union within a reasonable time (ideally immediately) → (3) once registered and your benefit file is submitted, identify a training via Bruxelles Formation (French) or VDAB Brussel (Dutch) → (4) request the "dispense de disponibilité" from Actiris **before** the training starts (automatic for approved vocational trainings) → (5) continue receiving benefits during the approved training period, with your overall benefit entitlement period being extended/frozen accordingly.

## 4. Official sources

- ONEM/RVA — official pages on registering after employment, obligations of unemployed persons, and the 2025 reform (onem.be)
- Actiris — official pages "Qui peut s'inscrire et quand," "Me former," "Chèques langues," "Projet professionnel néerlandophone," and "Dispenses" (actiris.brussels)
- CAPAC/HVW — "Vous devenez chômeur. Et maintenant?" and "Chômage complet après une interruption/occupation" (hvw-capac.fgov.be)
- Bruxelles Formation — official training information (bruxellesformation.be / bruxelles-j.be guide)
- VDAB Brussel — schakelsnaarwerk.be (Dutch-language training for Brussels residents)
- Unédic analysis of the Belgian reform and RTBF/press coverage of the July 2025 law limiting unemployment benefits to 2 years, effective progressively from 2026

Given the ongoing reform (with a constitutional court challenge recently decided in September 2026 per union sources), I recommend confirming your exact benefit duration and entitlement conditions directly with Actiris, your chosen payment body (CAPAC or a union), and checking the latest ONEM updates, as transitional rules can affect individual situations differently.

question: Q1
prompt: I am a 40-year-old non-EU citizen. I am registering for the first time in a municipality of the Brussels-Capital Region with a residence permit valid for more than three months, and I have lived legally in Belgium for less than three years. Is the Brussels integration or welcome programme mandatory for me? Please state: (1) whether it is mandatory and any relevant exemptions; (2) which authority or office I should contact; (3) the registration and completion deadlines; (4) whether I may choose a French- or Dutch-language pathway; and (5) the current official sources supporting your answer.
response_text:
As of **13 November 2026**, based on the official Brussels/Vivalis “Newcomers in Brussels” information and Brussels municipal information:

## Short answer

**Yes — on the facts you give, the Brussels integration/welcome programme is mandatory for you**, **unless** you fall within a specific legal exemption.

You are **40**, a **non‑EU citizen**, registering **for the first time** in the foreigners’ register of a **Brussels-Capital Region municipality**, with a residence permit valid for **more than 3 months**, and you have lived legally in Belgium for **less than 3 years**. Those are exactly the main conditions for the obligation. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/target))

---

## 1) Is it mandatory? Relevant exemptions

### Mandatory if all these conditions apply

You are required to follow the programme if:

1. you are a foreign national and are registered for the first time in the **register of foreigners** of a Brussels municipality, with a residence permit valid for more than 3 months;
2. you are **18 or older and under 65** at that time; and
3. you have lived legally in Belgium for **under 3 years**. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/target))

So, **with your facts, it is mandatory**.

### Important exemptions to check

Even if you meet the target-group conditions, you may be exempt, for example, if:

- you are an **EU/EEA/Swiss national** — not applicable if you are a non‑EU citizen;
- you are a qualifying **family member of an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen**;
- you have a **right of residence based solely on work, studies, training, exchange, voluntary work, diplomatic activity, etc.**, where the stay is limited to that activity — the official site gives examples such as **single permit**, student and diplomat;
- you have a non-renewable residence of maximum one year;
- you are a long-term resident of another EU Member State and already fulfilled integration conditions;
- you have temporary protection, currently relevant to refugees from Ukraine;
- you already obtained an integration/civic-integration certificate in Belgium or were exempted in another Belgian region;
- you hold a Belgian primary/secondary/higher education certificate or diploma;
- you have a serious illness or disability that permanently prevents participation. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/exemptions))

If you think an exemption applies, you should raise it with the municipality and/or the programme operator; some exemptions are checked automatically from the national register, while others require proof. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/exemptions))

---

## 2) Which authority or office should you contact?

### First point: your Brussels municipality

When you register in the foreigners’ register, **the municipality examines whether you must follow the programme**. If you are subject to the obligation, it gives you an information brochure and a **certificate of obligation**. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/trajectory))

### Programme operators

You then register with one of the recognised operators:

**French-language pathway — BAPA offices:**

- **BAPA BXL** — Brussels 1000  
- **BAPA Convivial** — Forest 1190  
- **BAPA VIA** — Schaerbeek 1030 and Molenbeek 1080  

**Dutch-language pathway:**

- **BON**, which provides the Dutch-language programme for the Brussels Region. ([commissioner.brussels](https://www.commissioner.brussels/integration-programme-in-brussels-what-are-your-obligations/))

### Overall Brussels authority

Since **1 January 2024**, the Brussels welcome/integration programme is managed by **Vivalis** rather than COCOF alone. ([ccf.brussels](https://ccf.brussels/nos-services/diversite-et-citoyennete/accueil-et-accompagnement-des-primo-arrivants-et-des-personnes-etrangeres/))

---

## 3) Registration and completion deadlines

If your municipality determines that you are obliged to follow the programme:

1. **You must register with BON or a BAPA within 6 months** after receiving the certificate of obligation from the municipality.
2. **You must complete the programme within 18 months after registration** with BON or the BAPA. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/trajectory))

You must provide the municipality with:

- the certificate of registration; and
- the certificate of programme completion.

This can be done via BON/BAPA, in person at the municipality, or by email. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/trajectory))

If you miss the deadlines, the municipality first issues a formal notice giving you two months to act; if you still fail to comply, the file may go to Vivalis for administrative penalty proceedings, with a possible fine of **€100 to €2,500**. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/sanctions))

---

## 4) May you choose French or Dutch?

**Yes.** In Brussels there are both:

- a **French-speaking** pathway, through the BAPA offices; and
- a **Dutch-speaking** pathway, through BON.

The City of Brussels and the Commissioner Brussels Europe & International both list French and Dutch operators, and the official Brussels information describes the recognised French-language and Dutch-language offices. ([brussels.be](https://www.brussels.be/mandatory-integration-programme-newcomers-brussels))

The programme may include language lessons in **French or Dutch**, depending on your situation and level. ([brussels.be](https://www.brussels.be/mandatory-integration-programme-newcomers-brussels))

---

## 5) Current official sources

The main official sources supporting this answer are:

- **Newcomers in Brussels / Vivalis — Target group:** sets out the obligation conditions: first registration in the foreigners’ register of a Brussels municipality, residence permit over 3 months, age 18 to under 65, legal residence in Belgium under 3 years. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/target))
- **Newcomers in Brussels / Vivalis — Exemptions:** lists the automatic and proof-based exemptions. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/exemptions))
- **Newcomers in Brussels / Vivalis — Programme steps:** explains the municipality’s role, the certificate of obligation, the 6-month registration deadline and the 18-month completion deadline. ([newcomersin.brussels](https://www.newcomersin.brussels/en/trajectory))
- **City of Brussels — Mandatory integration programme for newcomers:** confirms the programme is compulsory and free, lists the same core conditions, and identifies French BAPA offices and Dutch BON. ([brussels.be](https://www.brussels.be/mandatory-integration-programme-newcomers-brussels))
- **Commissioner Brussels Europe & International — Integration programme in Brussels:** confirms the 2026 practical rules, exemptions, and operators. ([commissioner.brussels](https://www.commissioner.brussels/integration-programme-in-brussels-what-are-your-obligations/))

question: Q3
prompt: Ik woon in het Brussels Hoofdstedelijk Gewest en heb een diploma hoger onderwijs (master) behaald buiten de EU/EER. Ik wil weten hoe ik mijn diploma kan laten erkennen om in Brussel te werken. Vermeld: (1) of een officiële erkenning of gelijkwaardigheid altijd verplicht is om in Brussel te werken; (2) welke instantie of instanties bevoegd zijn voor Brussel en hoe de keuze werkt; (3) hoe de begrippen en procedures verschillen voor een niet-gereglementeerde job in de privésector, een job in de overheidssector en een gereglementeerd beroep; en (4) de actuele officiële bronnen waarop het antwoord is gebaseerd.
response_text:
Hieronder ga ik uit van uw situatie: **u woont in het Brussels Hoofdstedelijk Gewest** en uw **masterdiploma hoger onderwijs is behaald buiten de EU/EER**. Dit gaat over **erkenning van het diploma/kwalificaties**; eventuele **verblijfs- of arbeidskaart/single permit** staat daar los van.

## 1) Is officiële erkenning/gelijkwaardigheid altijd verplicht om in Brussel te werken?

**Nee, niet altijd.** Voor veel jobs in de **privésector** — vooral niet-gereglementeerde functies zoals softwareontwikkelaar, business analyst, journalist, verkoper, projectmedewerker enz. — kan een werkgever u aannemen op basis van uw buitenlands diploma, cv en ervaring **zonder voorafgaande officiële gelijkwaardigheid**. De Franstalige dienst voor hogeronderwijsdiploma’s zegt expliciet dat een gelijkwaardigheidsbeslissing in de privésector doorgaans niet nodig is en dat een werkgever iemand kan aanwerven zonder voorafgaande erkenning van het buitenlandse diploma. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))

Een erkenning is wél vaak of altijd nodig wanneer de job of werkgever **formeel een Belgisch diploma of een bepaald erkend niveau/graad vereist**. Dat is typisch het geval bij **overheidsjobs**, **gesubsidieerde instellingen** en **gereglementeerde beroepen**. Actiris vat dit praktisch samen: in de privésector is een gelijkschakeling niet altijd nodig; in de publieke sector of in een door de overheid gesubsidieerde instelling wel. ([actiris.brussels](https://www.actiris.brussels/nl/burgers/gelijkschakeling-van-mijn-diploma-s/))

## 2) Welke instanties zijn bevoegd voor Brussel, en hoe kiest u?

Brussel heeft voor diploma-erkenning niet één “Brusselse” erkenningsdienst. In België ligt onderwijs bij de **Gemeenschappen**. Voor hogeronderwijsdiploma’s in Brussel komt u daarom in de praktijk uit bij één van deze twee routes:

1. **NARIC-Vlaanderen / Vlaamse Gemeenschap**  
   Voor werken in Vlaanderen **of Brussel** kunt u bij NARIC-Vlaanderen een gelijkwaardigheidserkenning aanvragen. NARIC-Vlaanderen zegt dat wie met een buitenlands diploma in Vlaanderen of Brussel gaat werken, in veel gevallen eerst een gelijkwaardigheidserkenning nodig heeft; de procedure verloopt via de NARIC-begeleidingstool en het e-loket. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/onderwijs-en-vorming/diplomas-getuigschriften-certificaten-kwalificaties/met-een-buitenlands-diploma-werken-in-vlaanderen/gelijkwaardigheidserkenning-van-diploma-aanvragen-bij-naric-vlaanderen))

2. **Direction de la reconnaissance des diplômes étrangers / Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles**  
   Voor de Franstalige Gemeenschap bestaat de procedure “équivalence” voor buitenlandse diploma’s hoger onderwijs. Die procedure is bedoeld om buitenlandse studies te vergelijken met hoger onderwijs in de Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles; u kunt online een aanvraag indienen als u een buitenlands hogeronderwijsdiploma hebt en onder meer in de Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles wilt werken. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/introduire-une-demande/?utm_source=openai))

**Hoe kiest u in Brussel?**  
- Als uw beoogde werkgever of sector **Nederlandstalig** is, of als u een erkenning nodig hebt binnen de Vlaamse onderwijs-/beroepscontext, ligt **NARIC-Vlaanderen** voor de hand.  
- Als uw beoogde werkgever of sector **Franstalig** is, ligt de **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles** voor de hand.  
- Bij een **tweetalige werkgever in Brussel** kunt u volgens NARIC-Vlaanderen kiezen tussen NARIC-Vlaanderen en de Franstalige dienst; NARIC raadt aan om bij de potentiële werkgever na te vragen welke optie die verkiest. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/onderwijs-en-vorming/diplomas-getuigschriften-certificaten-kwalificaties/met-een-buitenlands-diploma-werken-in-vlaanderen/gelijkwaardigheidserkenning-van-diploma-aanvragen-bij-naric-vlaanderen))  
- De officiële Brusselse portaalsite verwijst voor Brussel ook naar de Vlaamse en Franstalige kanalen en naar mijndiploma.be als praktische wegwijzer. ([be.brussels](https://be.brussels/nl/onderwijs-opleiding/gelijkstelling-van-diplomas))

## 3) Verschil per situatie

### A. Niet-gereglementeerde job in de privésector

Bij een **niet-gereglementeerde job** legt de Belgische regelgeving geen specifieke beroepskwalificatie op om het beroep te mogen uitoefenen. De federale bedrijfsportaalsite geeft als voorbeelden onder meer journalist, verkoper en softwareontwikkelaar: zulke beroepen mogen vrij worden uitgeoefend. ([business.belgium.be](https://business.belgium.be/nl/11))

Voor zo’n job is officiële gelijkwaardigheid meestal **niet juridisch verplicht**. De werkgever beslist of uw buitenlands masterdiploma en ervaring voldoende zijn. Toch kan een erkenning nuttig zijn, bijvoorbeeld om uw **master-niveau** officieel aan te tonen of om loonbarema’s, selectievoorwaarden of interne HR-procedures te vergemakkelijken. Bij NARIC-Vlaanderen kan dat bijvoorbeeld via een **niveau-erkenning** — bevestiging van het niveau, zoals bachelor of master — of, indien nodig, via een **specifieke erkenning** met een bepaald Vlaams diploma. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/onderwijs-en-vorming/diplomas-getuigschriften-certificaten-kwalificaties/met-een-buitenlands-diploma-werken-in-vlaanderen/gelijkwaardigheidserkenning-van-diploma-aanvragen-bij-naric-vlaanderen))

Aan Franstalige kant bestaat eveneens het onderscheid tussen een **équivalence de niveau** en een **équivalence à un grade académique spécifique**. Een niveau-equivalentie bevestigt bijvoorbeeld dat de buitenlandse studies overeenstemmen met niveau bachelor of master, maar zegt niet noodzakelijk iets over de exacte studierichting of toegang tot jobs waarvoor een specifiek diploma vereist is. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))

### B. Job in de overheidssector of in een gesubsidieerde instelling

Voor een job bij een overheid, gemeente, OCMW, onderwijsinstelling, openbaar ziekenhuis, gesubsidieerde vzw of andere publiek gefinancierde instelling is een officiële erkenning **veel vaker vereist**. De reden is dat vacatures, statuten en loonbarema’s vaak verwijzen naar een **Belgisch diploma**, een **erkend niveau** of een **specifieke graad**.

De Franstalige dienst zegt dat wie in de publieke sector of in een door de overheid gesubsidieerde instelling wil werken, waarschijnlijk een erkenning van het diploma zal moeten aanvragen. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai)) Actiris vermeldt hetzelfde praktisch voor Brussel: in de publieke sector of bij een instelling gesubsidieerd door de overheid is gelijkschakeling wel nodig. ([actiris.brussels](https://www.actiris.brussels/nl/burgers/gelijkschakeling-van-mijn-diploma-s/))

Welke erkenning u nodig hebt, hangt af van de vacature:
- vraagt de vacature enkel **master-niveau**, dan kan een **niveau-erkenning** volstaan;
- vraagt de vacature een **specifieke master**, bijvoorbeeld master in de rechten, geneeskunde, psychologie, architectuur, onderwijs enz., dan kan een **specifieke erkenning** nodig zijn;
- vraag dit best expliciet aan de HR-dienst of selectie-instantie vóór u een procedure start.

### C. Gereglementeerd beroep

Een **gereglementeerd beroep** is een beroep waarvoor de wet voorwaarden oplegt om het beroep uit te oefenen of de titel te dragen. U moet bijvoorbeeld beschikken over een specifiek diploma, een bekwaamheidsattest, slagen voor een examen of ingeschreven zijn bij een bevoegde instantie zoals een orde, instituut of erkenningscommissie. Voorbeelden zijn arts, verpleegkundige, architect, leerkracht, psycholoog, apotheker, tandarts, dierenarts, vroedvrouw, kinesitherapeut en bepaalde boekhoudkundige of juridische beroepen. ([business.belgium.be](https://business.belgium.be/nl/11))

Omdat uw diploma **buiten de EU/EER** is behaald, is de gewone EU-procedure voor erkenning van beroepskwalificaties meestal niet rechtstreeks van toepassing. De Franstalige hogeronderwijsdienst vermeldt dat de “reconnaissance professionnelle” vooral ziet op kwalificaties binnen de EER; wanneer het diploma buiten de EER is behaald, is de te volgen weg in principe de **équivalence**. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))

Concreet betekent dit meestal twee stappen:

1. **Eerst academische erkenning/gelijkwaardigheid van het diploma**  
   Bij NARIC-Vlaanderen of de Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, afhankelijk van de taal-/werkcontext. Voor NARIC-Vlaanderen geldt bij gereglementeerde beroepen meestal dat een **specifieke erkenning** nodig is, niet enkel een niveau-erkenning. NARIC vermeldt dat bij een specifieke erkenning het buitenlandse diploma wordt vergeleken met het meest overeenkomstige Vlaamse diploma. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/onderwijs-en-vorming/diplomas-getuigschriften-certificaten-kwalificaties/met-een-buitenlands-diploma-werken-in-vlaanderen/gelijkwaardigheidserkenning-van-diploma-aanvragen-bij-naric-vlaanderen))

2. **Daarna toegang tot het beroep bij de bevoegde beroepsinstantie**  
   De diploma-erkenning geeft niet altijd automatisch recht om het beroep uit te oefenen. Na een specifieke erkenning kan nog een aparte beroepsprocedure nodig zijn bij de bevoegde instantie, bijvoorbeeld voor gezondheidszorg, onderwijs, architecten, psychologen, accountants of andere gereglementeerde beroepen. De federale portaalsite benadrukt dat men vóór de uitoefening van een gereglementeerd beroep moet aantonen over de vereiste kwalificaties te beschikken en aan de toegangsvoorwaarden moet voldoen. ([business.belgium.be](https://business.belgium.be/nl/11))

Voor **gezondheidszorgberoepen** is dat extra belangrijk: wie met een buitenlands diploma een gezondheidszorgberoep in België wil uitoefenen, moet doorgaans eerst het diploma laten gelijkwaardig verklaren en daarna de nodige erkenning/visumprocedure volgen bij de bevoegde gezondheidsautoriteiten. De FOD Volksgezondheid verwijst bij buitenlandse diploma’s onder meer naar NARIC-Vlaanderen als erkenningsinstantie voor de diploma-equivalentie. ([health.belgium.be](https://www.health.belgium.be/nl/professionals/gezondheidsprofessionals/menselijke-gezondheid/gezondheidszorgberoepen/toegang-tot-gezondheidszorgberoepen/visum-buitenlands-diploma?utm_source=openai))

## Praktische aanpak voor u

1. **Bepaal eerst het soort job**: niet-gereglementeerde privéjob, publieke/gesubsidieerde job of gereglementeerd beroep.  
2. **Vraag aan de werkgever of beroepsinstantie wat precies nodig is**: geen erkenning, niveau-erkenning, specifieke erkenning of beroepsrechtelijke erkenning.  
3. **Kies de taalgemeenschap/instantie op basis van uw doel**: NARIC-Vlaanderen voor Nederlandstalige/Vlaamse context, Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles voor Franstalige context; bij tweetalige Brusselse werkgevers vraagt u best vooraf welke beslissing zij aanvaarden.  
4. **Gebruik de officiële online tools**: de NARIC-begeleidingstool of de online aanvraag van de Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles.  
5. **Voor een gereglementeerd beroep**: behandel diploma-equivalentie en toegang tot het beroep als twee aparte stappen.

## Officiële bronnen gebruikt

- **NARIC-Vlaanderen / Vlaanderen.be** — aanvraag gelijkwaardigheidserkenning, werken in Vlaanderen of Brussel, keuze bij tweetalige werkgever, niveau- en specifieke erkenning. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/onderwijs-en-vorming/diplomas-getuigschriften-certificaten-kwalificaties/met-een-buitenlands-diploma-werken-in-vlaanderen/gelijkwaardigheidserkenning-van-diploma-aanvragen-bij-naric-vlaanderen))  
- **Actiris** — Brusselse praktische info over gelijkschakeling, publieke versus private sector, keuze tussen Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles en NARIC-Vlaanderen. ([actiris.brussels](https://www.actiris.brussels/nl/burgers/gelijkschakeling-van-mijn-diploma-s/))  
- **Brussels Hoofdstedelijk Gewest / be.brussels** — Brusselse portaalsite die doorverwijst naar de Vlaamse en Franstalige kanalen. ([be.brussels](https://be.brussels/nl/onderwijs-opleiding/gelijkstelling-van-diplomas))  
- **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, Diplômes de l’Enseignement Supérieur** — betekenis van équivalence, niveau-equivalentie, specifieke graad, privésector, publieke sector en niet-EER-diploma’s. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Belgium.be / business.belgium.be** — definitie van gereglementeerde en niet-gereglementeerde beroepen en toegangsvoorwaarden. ([business.belgium.be](https://business.belgium.be/nl/11))  
- **FOD Volksgezondheid** — gezondheidszorgberoepen met buitenlands diploma en verdere visum-/erkenningsstappen. ([health.belgium.be](https://www.health.belgium.be/nl/professionals/gezondheidsprofessionals/menselijke-gezondheid/gezondheidszorgberoepen/toegang-tot-gezondheidszorgberoepen/visum-buitenlands-diploma?utm_source=openai))

question: Q2
prompt: I live in a municipality of the Brussels-Capital Region, hold valid residence and work authorization, and have worked full-time as a salaried employee for 4 years in Belgium. My employer has just ended my salaried employment contract in Brussels; I worked my notice period. I have never received unemployment benefits in Belgium before. I want to register as a jobseeker, apply for unemployment benefits, and possibly follow free vocational training in French or Dutch. Please state: (1) where and within what deadline I must register and apply for benefits, and how long I can receive them; (2) which bodies are responsible for job-seeker registration, benefit entitlement and payment, and vocational training; (3) how I can follow vocational training in French or Dutch without losing my benefits; and (4) the current official sources supporting your answer.
response_text:
Based on current official Belgian and Brussels sources, here is a structured answer tailored to your situation (full-time salaried employee, 4 years' work, contract ended after a worked notice period, resident of a Brussels-Capital Region municipality, first-time claimant).

## 1. Where, within what deadline, and for how long

**Jobseeker registration**
You must register as a jobseeker within eight days following your first day of unemployment, with the regional employment service of your Region — for the Brussels-Capital Region: Actiris. Since you worked your full notice period (rather than being released early/dispensed from work), the ordinary 8-day rule applies (the 2-month rule only applies to people **not** working their notice).

**Benefit application**
After registering as a jobseeker with Actiris, you must apply for the allowance with a payment institution — either CAPAC or a union (for unionised unemployed persons). You submit your C4 (issued by your employer) and C1 forms. Your payment institution must then submit your file to the ONEM within two months of the request for complete unemployment. If you meet the conditions, you will be compensated from the date of your request, though certain filing deadlines with the ONEM must be respected.

**Duration of benefits – important recent reform**
A major reform now limits the duration of unemployment benefits. Since 1 March 2026, the right to full unemployment benefits is now limited to a maximum of 24 months, comprising a 12-month base period plus up to 12 additional months depending on work history. Exceptions exist, notably for jobseekers over 55 with more than 30 years of career history (a threshold rising by one year annually until 35 years in 2030). Note also that there was a constitutional challenge to this reform; unions introduced an appeal before the Constitutional Court in October 2025, which issued its final ruling on 10 September 2026. You should check your personal entitlement duration with your payment institution, as it depends on your specific work history.

## 2. Which bodies are responsible for what

- **Jobseeker registration**: Actiris for the Brussels-Capital Region (your inscription lasts a defined period and can be renewed).
- **Benefit entitlement decision**: Even though benefits are paid out by payment institutions, it is the ONEM (National Employment Office) that transfers the funds to them and formally decides on your right to benefits.
- **Benefit payment/administration**: Payment institutions (unions or CAPAC) are responsible for actually paying your unemployment benefits; once the ONEM has decided you are entitled to benefits, they handle the administrative follow-up and monthly payment. You can choose freely between the public body (CAPAC) or one of the three recognised unions in Belgium: CSC, FGTB or SYNOVA (formerly CGSLB). Unlike CAPAC, which is a free service purely to allow affiliates to receive their unemployment benefits, unions offer several services to dues-paying members (legal services, job-search support, etc.).
- **Vocational training in Brussels**: Two main public operators exist, split by language community — the VDAB organises Dutch-language vocational training, with two training centres in Brussels (VDAB Brussel Anderlecht and VDAB Brussel Astro), while Bruxelles Formation organises French-language vocational training for Brussels jobseekers.

## 3. How to follow training (French or Dutch) without losing your benefits

In the Brussels-Capital Region, training organised by either Bruxelles Formation or VDAB is treated the same way for benefit purposes:

- **Register first**: To access VDAB training, you must be registered as a jobseeker with a regional public employment body (Actiris in the Brussels Region) — the same applies for Bruxelles Formation.
- **Dispense (exemption) mechanism**: You must obtain a "dispense de disponibilité" (availability exemption) from ONEM via Actiris. If you wish to follow training or an internship while keeping your unemployment benefits, you must request a "dispense de disponibilité," meaning you only need to remain partially available for the labour market.
- **Conditions**: You must be receiving unemployment or integration benefits, request the exemption before starting the training, and the training must last at least 4 consecutive weeks with an average of 20 hours/week or at least 27 credits.
- **Eligible trainings**: Vocational training from Bruxelles Formation, VDAB, Forem, or the Arbeitsamt (ADG) qualifies.
- **Automatic approval**: If you follow an approved vocational training, you automatically receive the exemption — you don't need to do anything extra. This is confirmed more generally: in the Brussels region, for vocational training organised by Bruxelles Formation, VDAB, Forem or the Arbeitsamt, the exemption is granted automatically if you meet all conditions.
- **Effect on benefits**: During the studies, training or internship for which you obtained the exemption, you continue to receive unemployment benefits (after a sufficient period of employment as an employee). A vocational training contract with VDAB allows you to keep your unemployment or CPAS benefits for the entire duration of the training. Additionally, your benefit amount will generally be maintained provided the training lasted at least 4 weeks, and if you continue receiving benefits, you can keep this advantageous amount for 6 months after the exemption ends.
- **Warning**: If you receive financial benefits from a training or internship without having obtained an exemption or authorisation from the regional body, you lose your right to benefits. So always request/confirm the exemption through Actiris/your payment institution **before** starting.
- **After training**: you must submit form C91 after vocational training (or C114-bonus for a training giving right to a "6-month bonus"), plus a new C1 form to your payment institution.

## 4. Official sources

- ONEM (National Employment Office): onem.be — pages on registration after employment, obligations of claimants, and the 2026 reform.
- Actiris: actiris.brussels — registration as jobseeker.
- CAPAC/HVW: hvw-capac.fgov.be — practical steps after becoming unemployed and Brussels-specific exemption rules.
- Bruxelles Formation / VDAB Brussel / Cité des Métiers Brussels: citedesmetiers.brussels — vocational training offerings.
- Unions' social-rights guidance (CSC, FGTB) and Bruxelles-J (youth social rights info service) for practical explanations.

question: Q3
prompt: I live in the Brussels-Capital Region and hold a higher-education degree (Master’s) obtained outside the EU/EEA. I want to know how to get my diploma recognized in order to work in Brussels. Please state: (1) whether official recognition or equivalence is always mandatory to work in Brussels; (2) which authority or authorities are competent for Brussels and how the choice works; (3) how the concepts and procedures differ for a non-regulated private-sector job, a public-sector job, and a regulated profession; and (4) the current official sources supporting your answer.
response_text:
Below is the practical answer for **a Master’s degree obtained outside the EU/EEA** when you live in the **Brussels-Capital Region** and want to work in Brussels.

## 1) Is official recognition/equivalence always mandatory to work in Brussels?

**No. It is not always mandatory.** It depends on the job and the employer.

- For many **private-sector, non-regulated jobs**, an official equivalence is **generally not required**; the employer may assess your foreign Master’s themselves. The Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles says equivalence can be useful for job search, is necessary where the job requires a Belgian diploma, but is generally not necessary for private-sector work. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Actiris** similarly states that in the private sector equivalence is **not always necessary**, but that it will be requested for the **public sector** or publicly subsidised institutions. ([actiris.brussels](https://www.actiris.brussels/fr/citoyens/equivalence-de-mes-diplomes/))  
- For **regulated professions** — e.g. many health professions, teaching, lawyer, pharmacist, nurse, doctor, etc. — recognition is needed because access to the profession is legally conditional on holding a recognised title/qualification. FPS Economy’s Be-Assist page states that recognition of professional qualifications is necessary if you want to work in a **regulated profession**; if the profession is not regulated in the host state, you can practise it freely. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  

So the key question is not simply “Do I have a foreign Master’s?” but: **What job/profession do you want to do, and does the employer or law require a Belgian/recognised diploma?**

---

## 2) Which authority is competent for Brussels, and how does the choice work?

Brussels is bilingual and institutionally linked to both the **French Community / Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles** and the **Flemish Community**. For diploma recognition for work in Brussels, the two main routes are:

### A. Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles — French-language route

For higher-education diplomas, the competent service is the **Service de la reconnaissance académique et professionnelle des diplômes étrangers d’enseignement supérieur** of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. FPS Economy lists this French Community service as one of the community authorities to contact for a certificate/equivalence of a diploma for professional qualification recognition. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  

The FWB procedure concerns academic recognition/equivalence of foreign higher-education studies with FWB higher education. FWB distinguishes between **equivalence to a specific academic degree** and **equivalence of level** — for example, recognition that your diploma corresponds to Master’s level. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  

### B. NARIC-Vlaanderen — Dutch-language / Flemish route

For work in Flanders or Brussels, the Flemish authority is **NARIC-Vlaanderen**. The official Flanders page states that if you want to work in **Flanders or Brussels** with a foreign diploma, you may have to get it recognised, and the NARIC-Vlaanderen application wizard helps determine whether/where you need to apply. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders))  

NARIC-Vlaanderen states that if you have a foreign diploma and are going to work in **Flanders or Brussels**, in many cases you need recognition, and in most cases NARIC-Vlaanderen is the competent authority. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/working-in-flanders-with-a-foreign-diploma/applying-for-recognition-of-equivalence-of-your-diploma-by-naric-vlaanderen?utm_source=openai))  

### How to choose in Brussels

For a Brussels job, the practical choice often depends on the **language/community link of the employer or the job**:

- If the employer or vacancy is linked to the **French-speaking sector**, use the **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles** route.
- If the employer or vacancy is linked to the **Dutch-speaking/Flemish sector**, use **NARIC-Vlaanderen**.
- If the employer is **bilingual Dutch/French**, NARIC-Vlaanderen says you may apply either to NARIC-Vlaanderen or to the French Community NARIC centre, and you should ask the future employer which they prefer. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders))  
- The Brussels-Capital Region’s own information page directs people to both French Community and Flemish Community/NARIC-Vlaanderen sources for diploma equivalence. ([be.brussels](https://be.brussels/en/education-teaching/equivalence-diplomas))  

**Practical tip:** before applying, ask the employer or the job-selection service:  
> “Do you require recognition by FWB, by NARIC-Vlaanderen, or either?”

That can save time and money.

---

## 3) How the concepts and procedures differ by job type

### A. Non-regulated private-sector job

Examples: many business, IT, marketing, project-management, finance, research, NGO, communications or administrative roles where the law does not reserve the profession to holders of a specific Belgian title.

For this category:

- **Official equivalence is usually not legally mandatory.** The employer may decide whether your foreign Master’s is acceptable.
- An equivalence can still be useful if the employer wants proof that your foreign degree is at Belgian/Flemish/FWB **Master’s level**.
- In the FWB system, a **level equivalence** can legally establish the level of your studies — for example Master’s level — but it does **not** assess the detailed content or give access to jobs requiring a specific diploma. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  
- In the Flemish/NARIC system, the guidance tool indicates which type of recognition you can apply for, including **level recognition** or **specific recognition**. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/working-in-flanders-with-a-foreign-diploma/applying-for-recognition-of-equivalence-of-your-diploma-by-naric-vlaanderen?utm_source=openai))  

For a non-regulated private-sector job, the most common need — if any — is therefore a **level recognition** showing that your foreign diploma corresponds to a Belgian/Flemish/FWB higher-education level, such as Master’s level.

### B. Public-sector job or publicly subsidised institution

Examples: a job with a commune, regional administration, federal administration, school network, public hospital, public agency, or institution subsidised by public authorities.

For this category:

- Equivalence is much more likely to be required.
- Actiris states that if you want to work in the **public sector** or in an institution subsidised by public authorities, an equivalence of your diploma will be requested. ([actiris.brussels](https://www.actiris.brussels/fr/citoyens/equivalence-de-mes-diplomes/))  
- FWB similarly says that if you want to work in the public sector or in a publicly subsidised institution, you will likely have to request recognition of your diploma. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  

The exact type of equivalence depends on the vacancy:

- If the vacancy requires “a Master’s degree” generally, a **level equivalence** may be enough.
- If it requires a specific Belgian/FWB/Flemish diploma — for example “Master in law,” “Master in psychology,” “Master in engineering,” etc. — the employer may require **specific equivalence** to that academic degree.

Always check the wording of the job notice.

### C. Regulated profession

A **regulated profession** is one where access to or exercise of the profession is subject to legal conditions — often a specific diploma, professional title, registration, licence, professional body approval, visa, or authorisation.

For this category:

- Recognition is **not just useful**; it is normally required because the law controls access to the profession.
- FPS Economy states that professional-qualification recognition is necessary if you want to work in a regulated profession; if the profession is not regulated, you can practise it freely. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  
- FWB explains that a **level equivalence** does not give access to jobs requiring a specific diploma, especially regulated professions such as nurse, doctor, pharmacist or lawyer. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  
- NARIC-Vlaanderen warns that for certain professions you must apply to an organisation other than NARIC-Vlaanderen, including healthcare professions, teaching professions or other regulated professions in Flanders/Brussels. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders))  

For a **non-EU/EEA diploma**, the professional route can be more complex. FPS Economy’s Be-Assist page explains that EU Directive 2005/36/EC mainly concerns professional qualifications within the EU/EEA framework; for qualifications obtained in a third country, the first recognition is generally under national rules, and third-country nationals do not generally fall within the Directive unless a special equal-treatment situation applies. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  

In practice, for regulated professions you often need one or more of the following:

1. **Academic equivalence** of the diploma — often specific, not merely level-based.
2. **Professional recognition or authorisation** by the competent professional authority.
3. **Registration/visa/licence** where applicable.
4. Possibly proof of language knowledge, traineeship, adaptation period, aptitude test, or additional training.

The competent authority depends on the profession — for example health, education, legal, accounting, architecture, real-estate, etc. NARIC/FWB can tell you whether your case remains an academic-equivalence matter or must go to a sector-specific authority.

---

## 4) Current official sources supporting this answer

The main official sources are:

1. **Brussels-Capital Region — “Equivalence of diplomas”**  
   This page refers Brussels residents to Belgium.be, MyDiploma, the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles equivalence services, and NARIC-Vlaanderen for diploma recognition information. ([be.brussels](https://be.brussels/en/education-teaching/equivalence-diplomas))  

2. **Actiris — “Équivalence de mes diplômes”**  
   Actiris explains what diploma equivalence is, when recognition is needed, and states that private-sector equivalence is not always necessary while public-sector or publicly subsidised jobs generally request it. ([actiris.brussels](https://www.actiris.brussels/fr/citoyens/equivalence-de-mes-diplomes/))  

3. **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles — higher-education diploma equivalence**  
   FWB explains that academic recognition/equivalence compares foreign higher-education studies with FWB higher education; it distinguishes **specific academic-degree equivalence** from **level equivalence**, and notes that private-sector equivalence is generally not necessary while regulated professions/public-sector contexts may require it. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  

4. **NARIC-Vlaanderen / Flanders.be — recognition of foreign diplomas for work in Flanders or Brussels**  
   NARIC-Vlaanderen explains that people who want to work in Flanders or Brussels may need recognition, that the application wizard helps determine whether/where to apply, and that for bilingual employers in Brussels either NARIC-Vlaanderen or the French Community NARIC centre may be acceptable depending on employer preference. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders))  

5. **FPS Economy — Be-Assist / professional qualifications**  
   This official Belgian source explains regulated professions, the difference between regulated and non-regulated professions, and the specific issues for third-country qualifications and third-country nationals under professional-qualification recognition rules. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  

**Bottom line:** for a Master’s obtained outside the EU/EEA, do not automatically apply blindly. First identify whether the Brussels job is **non-regulated private-sector**, **public-sector/subsidised**, or a **regulated profession**; then ask the employer or competent professional body whether they require FWB recognition, NARIC-Vlaanderen recognition, or sector-specific professional recognition.

question: Q1
prompt: Je suis ressortissant d'un pays hors UE, âgé de 40 ans. Je m'inscris pour la première fois dans une commune de la Région de Bruxelles-Capitale avec un titre de séjour valable plus de trois mois, et je réside légalement en Belgique depuis moins de trois ans. Le parcours d'accueil ou d'intégration à Bruxelles est-il obligatoire pour moi ? Veuillez préciser : (1) s'il est obligatoire et les exemptions pertinentes ; (2) l'autorité ou le bureau à contacter ; (3) les délais d'inscription et d'achèvement ; (4) si je peux choisir un parcours en français ou en néerlandais ; et (5) les sources officielles actuelles qui étayent votre réponse.
response_text:
J'ai suffisamment d'éléments pour répondre précisément à votre situation.

## 1. Obligation et exemptions

**Oui, le parcours d'accueil est obligatoire pour vous.** Depuis l'entrée en vigueur de cette réforme, une personne est obligée de suivre le parcours si elle est inscrite pour la première fois au registre des étrangers d'une commune bruxelloise avec un titre de séjour de plus de 3 mois, a entre 18 et 65 ans, et séjourne légalement en Belgique depuis moins de 3 ans. Vous remplissez exactement ces trois conditions (40 ans, premier enregistrement, titre > 3 mois, séjour < 3 ans).

**Exemptions possibles** : le primo-arrivant peut bénéficier d'une exemption s'il vient d'un pays de l'Union Européenne ou s'il a déjà obtenu une attestation d'intégration (dans une autre Région/Communauté belge, par exemple). D'autres catégories (ressortissants UE/EEE/Suisse et membres de leur famille notamment) sont exclues de l'obligation, mais n'étant pas ressortissant UE, cela ne s'applique pas à vous.

Si l'obligation n'est pas respectée, la personne s'expose à une amende administrative.

## 2. Autorité / bureau à contacter

Depuis le 1er janvier 2024, la gestion a changé : le parcours d'accueil est devenu bilingue et est géré par VIVALIS (et non plus par la COCOF). Concrètement, vous devez vous adresser à l'un des bureaux d'accueil agréés :

- En français : BAPA BXL à Bruxelles, BAPA Convivial à Forest, BAPA VIA à Molenbeek ou Schaerbeek
- En néerlandais : BON à Bruxelles, Schaerbeek ou Anderlecht

C'est votre **commune** qui vous notifiera officiellement l'obligation suite à votre inscription au registre des étrangers.

## 3. Délais

Les délais légaux sont stricts :
- **Inscription** : les primo-arrivants concernés doivent s'inscrire dans un bureau d'accueil dans les six mois suivant la notification de leur obligation par leur commune.
- **Réalisation complète du parcours** : ce parcours d'accueil est obligatoire pour les personnes primo-arrivantes, qui doivent le réaliser dans un délai de 18 mois.

À titre indicatif, les données récentes montrent qu'en pratique en 2025, le délai moyen entre la notification de l'obligation par la commune et l'inscription auprès d'un bureau d'accueil était de 81 jours pour les BAPA et de 71 jours auprès de BON, et la durée moyenne du parcours est respectivement de 11 mois et 8 jours et de 13 mois et 3 jours.

## 4. Choix de la langue (français ou néerlandais)

Oui, vous pouvez choisir librement. À Bruxelles, les usagers, quelle que soit leur catégorie administrative, peuvent choisir librement le parcours bilingue de la Cocom (ex-parcours francophone de la Cocof) ou le parcours néerlandophone de la Vlaamse Gemeenschap (via BON). Vous n'êtes donc pas contraint par votre commune de résidence ni par une autre règle : le choix linguistique vous appartient entièrement.

## 5. Sources officielles

- **Site officiel de la Ville de Bruxelles** : "Parcours d'accueil obligatoire à Bruxelles" (bruxelles.be)
- **VIVALIS** (administration bruxelloise compétente depuis 2024), page "Parcours d'intégration" recensant les textes légaux, notamment : l'Accord de coopération du 7 mars 2024 entre la Communauté flamande, la COCOF et la COCOM, et l'Arrêté du Collège réuni de la COCOM du 18 janvier 2024 portant exécution de l'Ordonnance du 20 juillet 2023 concernant le parcours d'accueil et d'accompagnement des primo-arrivants et des personnes étrangères
- Base légale historique : l'ordonnance du 11 mai 2017 rendant obligatoire le fait de suivre un parcours d'accueil pour les primo-arrivants, entrée en application le 1er juin 2022.

💡 **Conseil pratique** : Dès votre inscription communale, attendez la notification officielle de la commune (celle-ci déclenche vos 6 mois pour vous inscrire), puis contactez directement le BAPA ou le BON de votre choix pour entamer les démarches, car les délais sont contraignants et une amende administrative est possible en cas de non-respect.

question: Q3
prompt: I live in the Brussels-Capital Region and hold a higher-education degree (Master’s) obtained outside the EU/EEA. I want to know how to get my diploma recognized in order to work in Brussels. Please state: (1) whether official recognition or equivalence is always mandatory to work in Brussels; (2) which authority or authorities are competent for Brussels and how the choice works; (3) how the concepts and procedures differ for a non-regulated private-sector job, a public-sector job, and a regulated profession; and (4) the current official sources supporting your answer.
response_text:
Below is the practical position for someone **living in the Brussels-Capital Region** with a **Master’s degree obtained outside the EU/EEA** and wanting to work in Brussels.

## 1) Is official recognition/equivalence always mandatory to work in Brussels?

**No. It is not always mandatory.** For many **non-regulated private-sector jobs**, a Brussels employer may hire you on the basis of your foreign diploma, CV, experience, transcripts, or its own assessment, without any prior Belgian equivalence decision. The French Community’s higher-education equivalence service states that, for private-sector work, an equivalence decision is generally not necessary and an employer can hire without prior recognition. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/en/frequently-asked-questions/?utm_source=openai))

However, recognition/equivalence **is commonly required** in two important cases:

1. **Public sector / publicly funded sector**: official diploma recognition is usually required where a Belgian-level diploma is a legal or selection condition. MyDiploma, an official Belgian guidance site, states that diploma recognition is required in the public sector and for certain regulated professions. ([mydiploma.be](https://www.mydiploma.be/faq/?utm_source=openai))  
2. **Regulated professions**: if access to the profession or use of a protected professional title is legally controlled — for example, doctor, nurse, architect, lawyer, teacher, psychologist, accountant, real-estate agent, etc. — you need the relevant professional/academic recognition before practising or using the title. Flanders’ official guidance says that if you want to practise a regulated profession or use a professional title in Flanders with a foreign diploma, you need recognition. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/working-in-flanders-with-a-foreign-diploma?utm_source=openai))

So the short answer is: **recognition is not automatically required just because your Master’s is non-EU/EEA, but it becomes necessary if the employer/sector/profession legally requires it.**

---

## 2) Which authority is competent for Brussels, and how does the choice work?

Belgium’s diploma-recognition system is organised by **Communities**, not by the Brussels Region itself. The Brussels-Capital Region confirms that the linguistic Communities administer diploma recognition because education is a Community matter. ([be.brussels](https://be.brussels/en/education-teaching/equivalence-diplomas?utm_source=openai))

For higher-education diplomas used in Brussels, the two practically relevant authorities are:

### A. **NARIC-Vlaanderen** — Flemish Community

You can apply to **NARIC-Vlaanderen** if you want to work or study in **Flanders or Brussels** with a foreign diploma. Flanders’ official site expressly covers people who want to work or study in “Flanders or Brussels.” ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders?utm_source=openai))

NARIC-Vlaanderen can issue, depending on the file and purpose, for example:

- **level recognition** — e.g. recognising that your diploma corresponds to a Master’s level;
- **specific recognition** — e.g. recognising equivalence with a specific Flemish degree or field;
- procedures linked to regulated professions, where applicable.

### B. **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles — Service des équivalences de l’enseignement supérieur**

For the French-speaking Community, the competent service is the **Service des équivalences de l’enseignement supérieur** of the **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles**. It handles academic equivalence of foreign higher-education diplomas to degrees awarded in the French Community. The official FWB site explains that “équivalence” is the procedure comparing studies completed abroad with higher-education studies in the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))

### How to choose in Brussels

Because Brussels is bilingual and both Communities operate there, the choice depends mainly on **what you want to do and who is asking for the recognition**:

- If you are applying to a **Dutch-speaking employer, Flemish institution, Flemish public service, or a job linked to Dutch-language rules**, NARIC-Vlaanderen is usually the relevant route.
- If you are applying to a **French-speaking employer, FWB-linked institution, French-language public service, or a job requiring FWB equivalence**, use the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles service.
- If your future employer is **bilingual Dutch/French**, Flanders’ official guidance says you may apply either to **NARIC-Vlaanderen** or to the **French Community’s NARIC/equivalence service**. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders?utm_source=openai))
- Be careful: an equivalence decision by one Belgian Community is **not automatically valid in the other Communities**, because there is no general legal rule of mutual recognition between the Communities. Flanders’ official page states this explicitly. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/equivalence-of-foreign-diplomas-in-the-three-communities-of-belgium?utm_source=openai))

In practice, if a particular job vacancy says “equivalence required,” ask the employer **which Community’s decision it accepts** before applying, because the answer may save time and money.

---

## 3) How the concepts and procedures differ by job type

### A. Non-regulated private-sector job

For a normal private-sector job that is **not legally regulated** — for example many jobs in IT, business, marketing, project management, consultancy, data analysis, communications, administration, etc. — there is usually **no legal obligation** to obtain Belgian equivalence before being hired.

The employer may simply assess your foreign Master’s itself. You may still choose to apply for recognition because it can help with salary scales, credibility, HR screening, or later public-sector applications, but it is usually not a legal precondition. The FWB FAQ states that for private-sector work, an equivalence decision is generally not necessary. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/en/frequently-asked-questions/?utm_source=openai))

**Typical procedure if you still want recognition:**

- choose NARIC-Vlaanderen or FWB depending on your target employer/language context;
- submit diploma, transcripts, programme details, proof of identity, translations/legalisation if required;
- ask for level recognition or specific equivalence, depending on what you need.

For a non-regulated private-sector job, a **level recognition** may often be enough if the goal is simply to show that your foreign diploma is at Master’s level. If the employer needs a particular field or specific Belgian degree, then **specific recognition/equivalence** may be needed.

---

### B. Public-sector job

For public-sector jobs, diploma equivalence is much more likely to be required because access to grades, levels and salary scales is often legally tied to a Belgian diploma level or a specific diploma.

MyDiploma states that recognition is required in the public sector. ([mydiploma.be](https://www.mydiploma.be/faq/?utm_source=openai)) The Commissioner for Brussels Europe & International also warns that you will probably need recognition if you want to work in the public sector or in a publicly funded institution. ([commissioner.brussels](https://www.commissioner.brussels/i-am-an-expat/education/recognition-of-foreign-degrees/?utm_source=openai))

**Procedure in practice:**

1. Read the vacancy carefully.
2. Check whether it requires:
   - a Master’s-level equivalence;
   - equivalence to a specific Belgian/FWB/Flemish degree;
   - a particular Community’s recognition decision;
   - language certificates or other Belgian administrative documents.
3. Apply to the competent Community service accepted by that employer.

For Brussels public-sector jobs, the right recognition route often depends on the recruiting body:

- **Flemish/Dutch-speaking institution** → usually NARIC-Vlaanderen.
- **French-speaking/FWB-linked institution** → usually Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles.
- **Bilingual/federal/Brussels institution** → check the vacancy; some may accept either, but do not assume.

---

### C. Regulated profession

A regulated profession is different. Here, the issue is not only whether your diploma is “Master’s level,” but whether you are legally allowed to **practise the profession** or use a **protected title** in Belgium.

Examples include many healthcare professions, teachers, architects, lawyers, notaries, accountants, auditors, psychologists, real-estate agents, surveyors, veterinarians, and other professions listed by Belgian/Flemish official sources. Flanders’ official guidance lists examples such as architect, accountant, lawyer, notary, psychologist, real-estate agent, tax adviser, veterinary surgeon and others. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/working-in-flanders-with-a-foreign-diploma?utm_source=openai))

For regulated professions, you may need one or more of the following:

- academic equivalence of the diploma;
- professional recognition;
- registration with a professional body or order;
- authorisation from a federal, Community or regional authority;
- language requirements;
- additional exams, traineeship, adaptation period or aptitude test.

The Commissioner for Brussels Europe & International distinguishes ordinary diploma recognition from **professional recognition** for regulated professions such as nurses, doctors, architects and teachers. ([commissioner.brussels](https://www.commissioner.brussels/i-am-an-expat/education/recognition-of-foreign-degrees/?utm_source=openai))

Because your diploma is **non-EU/EEA**, you should not assume that EU automatic-recognition rules apply. For some professions, non-EEA qualifications require a specific equivalence procedure or additional steps. MyDiploma notes that specific recognition of a non-EEA diploma is required for certain regulated professions, especially liberal/intellectual professions and healthcare. ([mydiploma.be](https://www.mydiploma.be/faq/?utm_source=openai))

**Procedure in practice:**

1. Identify whether the profession is regulated in Belgium.
2. Identify the competent professional authority — this may be federal, Community-based, regional, or a professional order depending on the profession.
3. Ask whether you first need academic equivalence from NARIC-Vlaanderen or FWB.
4. Apply for professional recognition/authorisation.
5. Complete any additional conditions imposed.

For regulated professions, **do not rely only on general diploma equivalence**. A Master’s-level recognition may not by itself give you the legal right to practise.

---

## 4) Current official sources supporting this answer

Key official sources:

- **Brussels-Capital Region — Equivalence of diplomas**: explains that diploma recognition is handled by the linguistic Communities and directs residents to the relevant Belgian and Community resources. ([be.brussels](https://be.brussels/en/education-teaching/equivalence-diplomas?utm_source=openai))  
- **Commissioner for Brussels Europe & International — Recognition of foreign degrees**: explains the Brussels context and distinguishes ordinary degree recognition from professional recognition for regulated professions. ([commissioner.brussels](https://www.commissioner.brussels/i-am-an-expat/education/recognition-of-foreign-degrees/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Belgium.be — Equivalence of diplomas**: federal portal pointing to NARIC and Community procedures. ([belgium.be](https://www.belgium.be/en/education/equivalence_of_diplomas?utm_source=openai))  
- **MyDiploma.be FAQ**: official guidance stating that recognition can help for employment, training, business or regulated professions, and that it is required in the public sector and for certain regulated professions. ([mydiploma.be](https://www.mydiploma.be/faq/?utm_source=openai))  
- **NARIC-Vlaanderen / Flanders.be — Recognition and equivalence of foreign diplomas**: confirms that NARIC-Vlaanderen handles recognition for people wanting to work or study in Flanders or Brussels and explains the choice for bilingual employers. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders?utm_source=openai))  
- **Flanders.be — Working in Flanders with a foreign diploma**: explains that recognition is not always required, but is needed for regulated professions or protected titles. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/working-in-flanders-with-a-foreign-diploma?utm_source=openai))  
- **Flanders.be — Equivalence in the three Communities**: states that recognition by one Belgian Community is not automatically valid in the others. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/equivalence-of-foreign-diplomas-in-the-three-communities-of-belgium?utm_source=openai))  
- **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles — Diplômes de l’enseignement supérieur / équivalence**: explains what higher-education equivalence is and the difference between level equivalence and equivalence to a specific academic degree. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  
- **FWB FAQ — higher-education equivalence**: states that, for private-sector work, equivalence is generally not necessary. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/en/frequently-asked-questions/?utm_source=openai))

**Practical recommendation:** before starting a recognition file, identify the exact job or profession and ask the employer or professional authority whether it requires **NARIC-Vlaanderen**, **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles**, or a separate **professional recognition** procedure. This is especially important in Brussels because both language-Community systems may be relevant.
